stories.author: Judd Legum
stories.title: PopInfo Weekly: Mailers, measles, and manta ray
stories.text: This week, Popular Information released PaidForBy.info , a web app that gives unprecedented insight into who is really sending you political mailers — and who is paying for it. Anyone can use it for free. All you have to do is take a photo of the front and the back of the mailer and upload it. It also works on YouTube and TV ads. For months, Republicans, including House Speaker Mike Johnson (R-LA) and President Trump, have been claiming that Americans’ opposition to data centers is being manufactured by China. The claim was popularized by a 2026 report by the Bitcoin Policy Institute, which has been cited by several Republicans. The report, however, does not provide any evidence China is driving opposition to data centers. Through Paid For By , Popular Information obtained a political mailer from V-PAC, a super PAC supporting Republican Vivek Ramaswamy’s campaign for governor in Ohio, attacking his Democratic opponent, Amy Acton. The mailer is rife with false and misleading claims. stories.title: Walmart Says It Prices Products, Not People. Its Patents Suggest Otherwise.
stories.text: Walmart serves 280 million shoppers a week and churned out more than $22 billion in profit in the last fiscal year. So, suffice it to say, I was floored – and maybe even a bit flattered – when the retail behemoth issued not one but two public responses in just over a week to the warnings I’ve made to shoppers about the retailer’s new surveillance pricing and price-gouging technologies in my new book and in recent interviews. In an open letter to customers from the CEO , followed by a letter from the company’s top PR executive addressing me directly, Walmart insists that it “price[s] products, not people” and argues that building technological capacity is not the same as deploying it. But here’s the problem: Walmart’s public assurances tell a very different story from the one buried in its patent filings. Walmart is pouring resources into developing and protecting the technology it needs to create intimate shopper profiles and use that data to shape what consumers pay. This week, our organization, Groundwork Collaborative, released a stunning analysis of more than 10 years of Walmart’s patent filings. stories.title: Joe Walsh: “Why Is the Democratic Party So Afraid to Fight?”
stories.text: Former Republican Congressman Joe Walsh went from Tea Party firebrand to Trump supporter to Never Trumper to Democrat. With the midterms weeks away, David Sirota asks him what Democrats should do if they win: stay with the establishment, or finally build a populist movement of their own. They get into why Walsh backed Trump in 2016 and what he now regrets, how the Tea Party turned into MAGA, why “electability” dominates Democratic primaries, what a President AOC would mean for a former Tea Party guy, and what role ex-Republicans and Never Trumpers should play in Democratic politics . They also compare notes on a 30-year-old shared history on the Illinois campaign trail that Walsh didn’t remember. stories.title: 14-Year-Old Girl Riding Home on a School Bus Killed by Saudi Coalition Strike in Yemen
stories.text: Story by Rachid Mohsen* SANA’A, Yemen—On the afternoon of October 5, 14-year-old Athir al-Amri had just taken the last exam of her first semester. She was on a school bus going home when an airstrike hit next to the bus as it drove through the Saawan area of eastern Sana’a, Yemen’s capital. Shrapnel struck her in the head, killing her, witnesses and relatives said. “She was planning to spend the holiday playing as all children do during school breaks,” her 35-year-old cousin, Mohammed Al-Lahida, told Drop Site News. “The shrapnel decapitated her. If her mother saw her body, she would die of grief.” Two of her classmates were also wounded, one of them gravely, in the strike by the Saudi-led coalition. Ansarallah, an armed group also known as the Houthis, seized the capital Sana’a in 2014. A Saudi-led coalition intervened in 2015 on the side of Yemen’s internationally recognized government. A civil war raged for eight years, killing tens of thousands and sparking one of the world’s worst humanitarian crises, until a fragile ceasefire was brokered in 2022. stories.title: Noura Erakat on Three Years of Genocide and the Board of Peace's "New World Order"
stories.text: Three years into Israel's genocide in Gaza, Palestinian human rights lawyer and legal scholar Noura Erakat argues that Donald Trump's Board of Peace is about more than Gaza: it's a blueprint for a new world order. Drop Site's Sharif Abdel Kouddous speaks with Erakat, a professor at Rutgers University, about her Boston Review essay, "Exit and Exception." Erakat argues that the Board of Peace matters less for whether it succeeds than for what it reveals: a political project, driven by market fundamentalists and a tech elite, to exit international law and popular democracy altogether. She traces that project from the charter cities and special economic zones championed by figures like Peter Thiel to Gaza, which the Board's charter designates as a special economic zone and where Palestinians are described as "Gazans" rather than a people with a right to self-determination. Israel, she argues, has long been the model, claiming that Palestine is a legal exception where the rules that apply everywhere else do not.
